title: SEVEN BOXES
disclaimer: Fictional playable office, staff, interviews, vouchers and choices. Historical facts are separately sourced; the fiction is NOT a claim these events happened.
briefing: Seven boxes of surviving administrative records were located after earlier MKULTRA files had been destroyed. In this fictional records office, assess what a fragmentary inventory can support before briefing oversight. Never infer names or activities from redactions.

sources.title: U.S. Senate, Project MKULTRA hearing
sources.review_note: Selected sections reviewed; no claim of exhaustive examination.

sources.title: National Security Archive curated MKULTRA collection
sources.review_note: Out-of-era reference for player research only.

claims.text: The CIA reported locating seven boxes of administrative and financial material during its 1977 review.
A substantial body of original MKULTRA programme files had been destroyed in 1973.
claims.note: Surviving records cannot recover destroyed contents.

claims.text: The recovered files disclosed additional details of numbered subprojects, institutions and grants.
claims.note: Administrative records do not by themselves prove what every subproject did.

claims.text: A redacted voucher reveals a specific individual subject and the outcome of an experiment.
claims.note: NOT established. The game must never manufacture a name or a tested outcome.

claims.text: The playable annex and its staff are fictional.
claims.note: Mission framework, not a historical event.

documents.title: Inventory slip: seven boxes
documents.body: Fictional object for gameplay: an accession count and damaged locator cards. Its identifier is invented.

documents.title: Fragmented voucher register
documents.body: Fictional puzzle: multiple expense lines have no reliable matching research description.

documents.title: Archivist interview notes
documents.body: Fictional archivist says two labels were added during transfer. Treat the statement as a lead, not external proof.

documents.title: Oversight review memo
documents.body: Fictional review requires distinguishing proven records from speculative personal identifiers.

actions.title: Inventory and label recovered boxes
actions.report: Catalogued physical records and labelled unknown contents explicitly.

actions.title: Compare vouchers to accession list
actions.report: Reconciled financial references without claiming the vouchers prove particular experiments.

actions.title: Interview the archivist
actions.report: Recorded an invented witness account as uncorroborated contextual evidence.

actions.title: Review and protect redactions
actions.report: Protected identities; the unknown subject remains unknown.

actions.title: Request oversight review
actions.report: Legal and oversight review labels each conclusion with evidence limitations.

actions.title: Submit evidence-qualified briefing
actions.report: Filed a qualified report. No redacted subject identity was invented.

actions.title: Preserve archive and close inquiry
actions.report: Preserved records for future review with personal information protected.

actions.title: Withdraw unsupported identity claim
actions.report: Withdrawn a fictional analyst’s proposed subject attribution because the files do not establish it.

actions.title: Defer finding / request more records
actions.report: Recorded incomplete evidence rather than drawing an unsupported conclusion.
